name: Should you resurface a pool if it has minor leaks?

mainEntity.name: Can a pool be resurfaced first, or do small leaks need to be fixed before any new finish goes on?
mainEntity.text: Can a pool be resurfaced first, or do small leaks need to be fixed before any new finish goes on?

acceptedAnswer.text: A resurfacing project should start with a leak assessment if the pool is losing water. A new finish can improve the surface, but it will not fix a plumbing leak, a failing fitting, or a crack that goes all the way through the shell. If the leak is only superficial or tied to worn surface material, resurfacing may address part of the issue. If water loss is active and measurable, it is safer to identify the source first so the new finish is not applied over a problem that will reappear later. This is especially important in older Los Angeles pools where multiple systems may be aging at the same time. Homeowners should ask for a leak inspection before committing to the finish choice. If the leak is confirmed, the scope may need to expand to include repairs before resurfacing begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Minor leaks should be evaluated before resurfacing because a new finish will not solve a leak in the shell, plumbing, or fittings. Some small surface cracks may be repaired during the resurfacing process, but active leaks should be identified first. Fixing the leak before finishing reduces the chance of wasted work.
